To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The Seller asserts these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened." Our playbook records **no** written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback on cap or claims period. Treat the preamble as a negotiating assertion, not an agreed position — the draft should be marked up in full. I recommend confirming with Amelia directly that no principal-level agreement was given before responding.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1), presented as "FINAL."
- *Buyer wants:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is our conditional fallback only, and no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the excess-only structure converts the basket into a permanent AUD 250,000 deductible.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months for general warranty claims; the sweep deleted.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" sweep.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the sweep would silently drag Title, Tax, IP and indemnity claims into the general regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, for "administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime — 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright.** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m for shares the Seller may not fully own and recover at most AUD 4.8m.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* No carve-out; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- *Recommendation:* **Insert an express, non-waivable fraud carve-out; reject the "all Claims of any nature" language.** This is a hard-line playbook item that no one on our side can waive, and the Seller's drafting would purport to limit liability for its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sched 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- *Buyer wants:* Specific fair disclosure only — each matter disclosed with sufficient detail to identify its nature and scope; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2; require a fair-disclosure standard tied to the specific disclosures in Section 2 onward.** Whole-data-room disclosure would strip the warranties of substantive value and shift all diligence risk to us.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- *Buyer wants:* Delete the blanket exclusion. Any residual qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, and seller-side knowledge qualifiers must reference named seller persons after reasonable enquiry. Never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable from the data room" combined with the general-disclosure regime would amount to a constructive-knowledge bar on effectively every warranty.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 admits no final written consent and no evidence of 11.3 conditions being satisfied is included.
- *Buyer wants:* A condition precedent requiring (a) effective consent under cl 11.2 AND (b) evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; make effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent a true CP.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and "consent on delivery" would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the CP.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m facility addressed by a release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the post-completion release; require payout, funds-flow repayment and releases at Completion.** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on foot and only a promise of release is unacceptable without an irrevocable undertaking and principal approval.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 AUD 420,000 completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 confirms the exclusion and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) either as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price or expressly seller-funded with a specific indemnity.
- *Recommendation:* **Insist on a specific line item or seller-funding covenant plus indemnity, including on-costs.** The bonuses are triggered by Completion and crystallise in the Company we are buying; silence in the funds flow means we pay them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* A broadened indemnity covering failure of title to the SOW3 Project Materials and consequential loss, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure (Seller to procure payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion). Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified.
- *Recommendation:* **Broaden the indemnity and add a pre-Completion deliverable of payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment.** The real exposure is non-transfer of IP, not merely the AUD 180,000 fee — and we have not independently verified whether that fee is actually outstanding.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* DD-006 is a "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sched 6). DL 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification not established.
- *Buyer wants:* Log preservation, a completed investigation, and update obligations through to Completion; a specific indemnity scoped to this incident; no acceptance of the "not material" characterisation.
- *Recommendation:* **Require preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity; do not accept the materiality characterisation.** Per our playbook we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss in either direction — the point is to preserve our position until the facts are in.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000, DD-008/DD-011) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8 is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Buyer wants:* Assessment of timing, terminability and accrual status before accepting any classification; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
- *Recommendation:* **Hold; request the renewal terms and reserve position.** Our playbook does not mandate a Debt classification or deduction, but the Seller's own disclosure declines to confirm ordinary course, so we should not concede it either.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 13); limitations/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax and IP folded into the general regime.
- *Buyer wants:* Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants each in their own regime with their own caps and periods; no general-regime override.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete the override language and insert an express clause that general limitations do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment or covenant claims.** These sweeps are the mechanism by which the Seller collapses every separate protection into the 20%/18-month box.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence of ownership, authority and absence of encumbrances — ASIC company extract and historical searches, PPSR search, share certificates, board/shareholder approvals, and a clean-title warranty uncapped per SPA-N-004.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not rely on DD-012; run independent searches and require title deliverables at Completion.** The register is an internal document supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above."
- *Buyer wants:* Both remain OPEN; separate Tax and IP regimes with their own caps and periods to be negotiated; no acceptance of unlimited liability either, but no acceptance of the general cap/18-month period.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "settled" characterisation; mark both as open items.** Nothing has been agreed on Tax or IP, and folding them into a 20%/18-month general regime would be a significant and unauthorised concession.

---

**Summary.** Of the 16 items, 14 should be rejected or materially marked up; two (Sandbar, Export incident) should be held pending further information with position reserved. The Disclosure Letter is actually helpful to us — Sections 2–10 confirm that none of the key completion deliverables (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment/assignment, independent title evidence) exist yet, which undercuts the Seller's "fair and balanced / FINAL" framing. I recommend we respond with a full mark-up and a short cover note recording that no principal-level agreement on cap or claims period has been given.
